Rashi on Pesachim 32b:10:1.english: And sins through error - It is written with regard to the misuse of consecrated property.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:10:2.hebrew: והלא דין הוא - דמזיד פטור מקרבן, ולמה לי קרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:10:2.english: Could this not be [derived through] an a fortiori inference - That an intentional [transgressor] is exempt from an offering, so why do I need a verse?

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:10:3.english: For which Scripture made [one] liable to karet - Such as [forbidden] fat and blood.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:10:4.hebrew: פטר בהן את המזיד - מקרבן, דגבי חטאת שגגה כתיב:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:10:4.english: Exempted the intentional [transgressor] in their case - From a sacrifice, as regarding a sin-offering, “error” is written.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:11:1.hebrew: לא חייב בהן מיתה - בידי שמים. אבל מעילה חייב על זדונה מיתה כדלקמן, ודילמא מיתה חמירא מכרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:11:1.english: Did not make [one] liable to death for them - [That is, death] at the hand of Heaven. But for misuse [of consecrated items], one is liable to death for its intentional [violation], as [explained] below; and perhaps death is more severe than karet.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:12:1.hebrew: ואמר ליה רב נחמן - גרסינן: האי תנא אלימא ליה כרת ממיתה מעיקרא — דקתני: מעילה שלא חייב בה כרת אלא מיתה כו', אלמא כרת חמירא; ולבסוף אלימא ליה מיתה — דקתני: תאמר במעילה כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:12:1.english: And Rav Naḥman said to him - The reading is: “This *tanna* initially considers *karet* stronger than death” — for he taught: “*Me’ilah*, for which [one] is not liable to receive *karet* but rather death...” etc., which shows that *karet* is more severe; “and subsequently he considers death to be stronger” — for he taught: “Shall you say regarding *me’ilah*...” etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:13:1.hebrew: וא"ל - רבי חייא: לעולם כרת אלימא ליה, והך סיפא דמתני' הכי קאמר: לא, אם אמרת בשאר מצות — שהרי לא חייב בהן אפילו מיתה בפחות מכזית, תאמר מעילה — שחייב בה מיהא מיתה בפחות מכזית. בכולהו גרסינן: ואמר ליה, ומתקיף ליה רב פפא כו' עד הדר ביה:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:13:1.english: And he said to him - Rabbi Ḥiyya [explained]: Actually, karet is more stringent to him, and this latter clause of the teaching is saying as follows: No, if you say with regard to other mitzvot — for [the Torah] did not obligate on them even death for less than an olive-bulk; shall you say with regard to misuse of consecrated property — where it obligated at least death for less than an olive-bulk? In all of them we read: “And he said to him”; and “Rav Pappa objected,” etc., until: “He retracted.”

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:13:2.hebrew: ומאי ניחותא - איכא? דהא רבה ורב ששת שדו ביה נרגא בהאי תירוצא דתריצית, ומקשו הכי: היכי אמרי' דתנא אפחות מכזית מחייב מיתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:13:2.english: And what settling [of the mind] - Is there? For Rabba and Rav Sheshet threw an axe at this resolution that I resolved, and they object as follows: How can we say that the Tanna holds [one] liable to death for less than an olive-bulk?

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:13:3.hebrew: מאן שמעת ליה דאמר מעילה זדונה מיתה רבי - ועל כרחך מתרומה גמר לה, כדמפרשינן. וכיון דמתרומה גמר, לא משכח בה מיתה אלא בכזית כתרומה, דתרומה גבי מיתה כתיב בה אכילה — דמיתה דתרומה נפקא לן מדסמיך "וכל זר לא יאכל קדש" גבי "ומתו בו כי יחללוהו", באלו הן הנשרפין בסנהדרין (דף פג:):
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:13:3.english: Who did you hear that said [that regarding] misuse, its intentional [commission incurs] death? Rabbi - And perforce, he derives it from terumah, as we explained. And since he derives it from terumah, he does not find [liability for] death in it except with an olive-bulk, like terumah, for regarding terumah, in connection with death, "eating" is written concerning it; as the death [penalty] for terumah is derived by us from the juxtaposition of: "No stranger shall eat of the holy thing" to: "and die therein, if they profane it," in [the chapter entitled] Elu Hen HaNisrafin in Sanhedrin (page 83b).

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:1:1.hebrew: אמר אביי ר' עקיבא ור' יוחנן בן נורי - אע"ג דאיחייב בתשלומין, סבירא להו דאין לו דמים; ובהא פליגי — רבי עקיבא ור' יוחנן בן נורי:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:1:1.english: Abaye said: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri - Even though [one who ate it] is obligated in payments, they hold that it has no monetary value; and in this do Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri disagree.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:4:1.hebrew: א"כ - דסבירא ליה מותר, ניהדר ליה ר' יוחנן לרבי עקיבא: ״אף לזה יש לו היתר הסקה״:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:4:1.english: If so - [If it is so] that he holds [benefit from chametz is] permitted, let Rabbi Yoḥanan respond to Rabbi Akiva: “Even for this, he has permission to kindle [it].”

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:4:2.english: An olive-bulk of teruma - [The baraita] refers to the rest of the days of the year.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:5:1.hebrew: פרט למזיק - תרומה של כהן, אפי' בשוגג, שאינו משלם חומש אלא קרן, כשאר מזיק חולין:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:5:1.english: To exclude one who damages - [The] teruma of a priest, even unwittingly, [teaching] that he does not pay an [additional] fifth, but rather [only] the principal, like any other damager of non-sacred property.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:6:1.english: That is necessary for an item that is fit to be sacred - And the entire verse was needed on account of its end.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:7:1.hebrew: דאית בה שוה פרוטה - וליכא כזית, כגון שנת בצורת:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:7:1.english: That it has the value of a peruta - And there is not an olive-bulk, such as [in] a year of drought.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:7:2.english: Since there is not an olive-bulk in it, etc. - For "eating" is written concerning it [which requires an olive-bulk].

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:8:1.hebrew: אמרוה רבנן קמיה דרב פפא - דקדקו מלבן, ואמרו לפניו: דהא מתני' דקפדא אכזית — דלא כאבא שאול; דהא שמעינן ליה דקפיד אפרוט', ולא אכזית:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:8:1.english: The Sages said it before Rav Pappa - They deduced [this] from their [own] minds and said before him that this Mishnah, which insists on an olive-bulk, is not in accordance with Abba Shaul; for we have heard him [say] that he insists on a peruta, and not on an olive-bulk.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:8:2.hebrew: תרתי בעי - שיהא בו כזית, דהא אכילה כתיבא ביה; ושיהא בדמיו פרוטה, דהא כתיב ונתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:8:2.english: Requires two [conditions] - That there must be an olive-bulk in it, since eating is written concerning it; and that its value must be a peruta, since it is written: “And he shall give.”

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:9:1.hebrew: חייב בתשלומין - אתרומת שוגג קאי, וקרן וחומש קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:9:1.english: Is liable to compensation - It refers to terumah [eaten] inadvertently, and it means [payment of] the principal and the [added] fifth.

Rashi on Pesachim 32b:9:2.hebrew: לענין מעילה - בנהנה מהקדש גבוה, דהתם לא כתיב אכילה. אבל לתרומה, אפי' יש בו שוה פרוטה, אין חייב חומש עד שיהא בו כזית. מכלל: לאבא שאול, אע"ג דליכא כזית. דאם איתא דתרתי בעי, וביש בו כזית קאי אבא שאול, וקאמר דאע"ג דאית ביה כזית בעינן פרוט' — הכי הוה להו למימר: כיון דיש בו כזית, חייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 32b:9:2.english: With regard to misuse - [This refers to] one who derives benefit from consecrated property of the Most High, as there "eating" is not written [in the Torah]. However, regarding teruma, even if it contains the value of a peruta, he is not liable [to add] a fifth until it contains an olive-bulk. By inference, according to Abba Shaul, [one is liable] even though there is no olive-bulk. For if it were so that he requires two [conditions], and Abba Shaul was speaking of [a case where] there is an olive-bulk, and was saying that even though it contains an olive-bulk we require [the value of] a peruta — this is what they should have said: "Since it contains an olive-bulk, he is liable."

Tosafot on Pesachim 32b:10:1.hebrew: מעילה שלא חייב בה כרת אינו דין שפטר בה את המזיד - תימה: נימא היא הנותנת, דשאר מצות שהן חמורות, שהן בכרת — אין לזדונה כפרה; אבל מעילה שהיא קלה, שאין בה כרת — יש לזדונה כפרה! וכה"ג איכא בריש מכות (דף ב:), דקאמר ק"ו: "ומה הוא שעושה מעשה, במזיד אינו גולה — עדים שלא עשו מעשה, אינו דין שלא יגלו?" — "היא הנותנת! הוא שעשה מעשה, במזיד לא יגלה — כי היכי דלא תיהוי ליה כפרה; הן שלא עשו מעשה — יגלו, דתיהוי להו כפרה!" ועוד, ארבעה המביאין על הזדון כשגגה יוכיחו, דאין בהן כרת וחייבין על זדונם: הבא על שפחה חרופה, ונזיר טמא, ושבועת העדות והפקדון (תוספתא דכריתות פ"א). ואומר ר"י, דשפיר פריך; בלאו הכי: "לא, אם אמרת וכו'". ומיהו, קשה לר"י: אמאי איצטריך בכריתות (דף ט.) בשפחה חרופה "אשר חטא" לרבות זדון, וגבי נזיר נמי דריש מ"פתאום" לרבות זדון? דאי משום דלא נילף ממעילה דאמעיט מזדון — אדרבה, משבועת העדות והפקדון אית לן למילף, דלחומרא מקשינן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 32b:10:1.english: Misuse [of consecrated property], which does not incur karet — is it not logical that it exempts one who acted intentionally? - It is astonishing! Let us say: On the contrary, that very [fact leads to the opposite conclusion]! For other mitzvot, which are stringent in that they [incur] karet, an intentional transgression has no atonement; but misuse [of consecrated property], which is lenient in that it does not [incur] karet, [perhaps] an intentional transgression should have atonement! And there is a similar case at the beginning of Makkot (2b), where it states an a fortiori inference: "Just as he who performs an action does not go into exile [if he killed] intentionally, is it not logical that [conspiring] witnesses who did not perform an action should not go into exile?" [And the Gemara answers:] "On the contrary! He who performed an action intentionally shall not go into exile, so that he will not have atonement; [whereas] they who did not perform an action shall go into exile, so that they will have atonement!" And furthermore, the four [transgressions where offenders] bring [an offering] for intentional [transgression] just like for unintentional [transgression] can prove [otherwise], as they do not [incur] karet and [yet offenders] are liable for their intentional [transgression]: one who has relations with a designated maidservant, and a defiled nazirite, and [one who takes a false] oath of testimony or [an oath concerning] a deposit (Tosefta Keritot, ch. 1). And the Ri says that it [the baraita] properly poses the question, [since] in any case [the baraita refutes it by saying]: "No, if you say etc." However, it is difficult for the Ri: Why was it necessary in Keritot (9a) regarding a designated maidservant [for the verse to state], "which he has sinned" [Leviticus 19:22], to include intentional [transgression], and regarding a nazirite too it deduces from "suddenly" [Numbers 6:9] to include intentional [transgression]? For if [one would suggest that the verses are necessary] so that we should not derive [an exemption] from misuse [of consecrated property], which excluded intentional [transgression] — on the contrary, we should derive from the oath of testimony and [the oath concerning] a deposit, for we compare toward stringency!

Tosafot on Pesachim 32b:5:1.hebrew: ואין נתינה פחות משוה פרוטה - ורבנן נמי לא פליגי אלא משום דכתיב אכילה. וא"ת: והא קיימא לן (חולין דף קלז:) דחטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי, אע"ג דכתיב בה נתינה, דכתיב: "תתן לו"? ובהזהב (ב"מ מז.) אמר: קונין בכלי אע"פ שאין בו שוה פרוטה, אע"ג דכתיב: "ונתן לרעהו"? וגבי גט נמי אמרינן (גיטין דף כ): כתבו על איסורי הנאה כשר, אע"ג דכתיב: "ונתן בידה"? ויש לומר: דהכא ודאי בעינן שוה פרוטה, דנתינה קיימא אתשלומין, והוי כמו השבת גזילה שאין בפחות משוה פרוטה; ולהכי, משום דכתיב "ונתן", משמע שפיר נתינה חשובה. אבל שאר מילי, אע"ג דכתיב בהן נתינה, לא בעינן שוה פרוטה. מיהו קשה לר"י: דרבי יהודה דריש בכריתות (דף ו:) "ואשר יתן ממנו על זר" בכזית, ויליף "נתינה" "נתינה" מתרומה; ואדיליף מתרומה בכזית, לילף מכל נתינה לחומרא דהוו בכל שהוא, כגון מתן דמים ומתן בהונות שאין בהן שיעור, והוי נמי דומי' דסיכה דהוי בכל שהוא! ולמ"ד התם נתינה בכל שהוא — א"ש:
Tosafot on Pesachim 32b:5:1.english: "And giving is not less than the value of a peruta" - And the Rabbis also disagree [with Abba Shaul] only because "eating" is written [in the verse, which requires an olive-bulk]. And if you say: But doesn't it stand established for us (Chullin 137b) that a single grain of wheat exempts the [entire] pile, even though "giving" is written regarding it, as it is written: "You shall give him" (Deuteronomy 18:4)? And in [the chapter entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47a), [the Gemara] says: One can acquire [by symbolic barter] with a utensil even though it does not possess the value of a peruta, even though it is written: "and gave it to his neighbor" (Ruth 4:7)? And regarding a bill of divorce as well, we say (Gittin 20a): If one wrote it on [an item from which] benefit is forbidden, it is valid, even though it is written: "and gives it into her hand" (Deuteronomy 24:1)? And it may be answered that here we certainly require the value of a peruta, because "giving" refers to payment [restitution], and it is like the return of a stolen item, which does not [apply to] less than the value of a peruta; and for this reason, since it is written: "and he shall give," it clearly implies a substantial giving [of monetary value]. However, in other matters, even though "giving" is written regarding them, we do not require the value of a peruta. However, it is difficult to the Ri: For Rabbi Yehuda expounds in Keritot (6b): "And whoever places [yiten, lit. gives] of it upon a stranger" (Exodus 30:33) — [is liable only] with an olive-bulk (kezayit), and he derives [this by a verbal analogy of] "giving" [from] "giving" from terumah. And instead of deriving from terumah [to require] an olive-bulk, let him derive from any [other] giving to be stringent, which are with any amount whatever — such as the placing of blood [on the altar] and the placing on the thumbs [and big toes of a metzora], which have no [minimum] measure — and it would also be similar to anointing, which is with any amount whatever! And according to the one who said there that [this] giving is with any amount whatever, it works well.

Tosafot on Pesachim 32b:6:1.hebrew: ההוא מיבעיא ליה לדבר הראוי להיות קודש - ואע"ג דמאת הקודש דרשינן דבר הראוי להיות קודש, אצטריך נמי "ונתן"; דאי כתב "את הקודש" לחודיה, ה"א דלא אתא למעוטי אלא מעות, אבל כל פירות ישלם. להכי כתב "ונתן", דמשמע שהפירות של נתינה בעינן ראוי להיות קודש:
Tosafot on Pesachim 32b:6:1.english: “That is necessary for an item that is fit to be consecrated” - And even though from “the holy thing” we derive that it must be an item that is fit to be consecrated, the word “and he shall give” was also necessary; for if it had written only “the holy thing,” I would have said that it came to exclude only money, but he must pay with any produce. For this reason it wrote “and he shall give,” which implies that regarding the produce of the giving, we require that it be fit to be consecrated.
